entries.note: Nat Med abstract, verbatim; untested as first use is right. model_filed=true unsupported: no FDA/EMA review names the AAV2/Chapel Hill dog model (AAV2-hFIX16 was never filed); set null. Mount 2002 figure in dose note unverified.

Abstract verbatim; the abstract itself sets dog long-term expression against the ~8-week human result, so comparison_stated=true holds. source_calls_it 'miss' is inferred; Mingozzi 2007 (10.1038/nm1549) says it outright: 'sustained in experimental animals but not in human subjects'.

Full text verbatim (Discussion). Macaque durability held. Per-dose level is unstated in Nathwani 2011 and 2014 NEJM (grepped), so correctly unscored; same-dose fact worth recording: 2x10^12 gave ~420% in macaques (Mol Ther 2011) vs 5.1%, off_by_>5x.
Abstract verbatim clause; untested correct. model_filed caveat as engagement 1.

Full text verbatim, but the sentence sits in the inhibitor/neoantigen paragraph and compares FIX-Padua specific activity (activity per antigen) with preclinical; no model-predicted level at 5x10^11 vg/kg is compared. Dose asks exposure, so strict reading is untested (drop entry). Not contra: no primary source states the macaque gap.

Abstract verbatim. Model here is intramuscular dogs while entries 2-3 use portal-vein dogs; year unchanged either way (Snyder 1999 is liver-directed, same year). Either cite Snyder here or treat IM as in-class and add Kay 2000 / Manno 2003 (see missing).
Abstract verbatim. contra holds only through the FIX-level surrogate (abstract reports no bleeding outcomes); scored consistently with entry 3. Rule question logged.

Full text verbatim. Macaques are not hemophilic, so 'as macaques predicted' is expression durability; the >90% bleeding cut is patient-only. same stands under the FIX surrogate and the follow-the-best-model reading; note should say surrogate.
Abstract verbatim; untested correct. 'No capsid T-cell response looked for' is drafter inference, acceptable as a note.

Abstract verbatim, but Manno's abstract calls the trial 'not associated with acute or long-lasting toxicity' and never mentions animals; contra rests on a drafter juxtaposition, failing rule 1. Mingozzi 2007 states it ('No such expansion occurs in mice'): move to 2007, comparison_stated true, subjects mixed.

Full text verbatim (Introduction); preceding sentence names 'elevations in serum liver enzymes, possibly as a result of a cellular immune response to the AAV8 capsid' in both high-dose patients, so it is the capsid transaminitis. Nathwani 2011 NEJM has no animal sentence, so 2014 is the right year. Model confirmed (Mol Ther 2011: 24 NHP, no capsid CTL, no toxicity).

missing: Intramuscular AAV2-FIX arm, if IM is in-class (efficacy #1 already uses the IM dog paper): Manno 2003 Blood 10.1182/blood-2002-10-3296 states 'effects gene transfer and expression in humans in a manner similar to that seen in animals' -> engagement same 2003 and safety same 2003 before the 2006 contra; Kay 2000 Nat Genet 10.1038/73464 states 'dose calculations based on animal data may have overestimated the amount of vector required' -> hedged dose comparison 2000. If IM is out-of-class, cite Snyder 1999 for efficacy #1 and say liver-directed in the context note.

Mingozzi 2007 Nat Med 10.1038/nm1549 (print 2007): the first primary source that states the AAV2 animal-vs-human miss in one sentence; should carry safety #2 (or at least be the supporting source for engagement #2).

Nathwani 2011 Mol Ther 10.1038/mt.2010.274 is the macaque model paper (24 NHP, 2x10^12 vg/kg -> 21 ug/ml ~420%, no capsid-specific CTL, no toxicity) and should be cited as the model source for the three 2014 entries; it also gives the same-dose magnitude (off_by_>5x) for the fact fields, which the draft under-reports by quoting the 22%-at-1x10^12 figure (Blood 2007, 10.1182/blood-2006-03-010181).

George 2017 full text restates the class-level safety miss ('the lack of animal models that recapitulate the human cellular immune response to the AAV capsid'); no new entry needed (status unchanged) but worth a note on safety #3 as the latest restatement.

FDA Hemgenix Summary Basis for Regulatory Action (fda.gov/media/164094) checked: NHP data summarised ('dose-dependent transgene expression... increased mean plasma FIX enzymatic and clotting activity compared to concurrent controls'), no NHP-vs-patient comparison, ALT elevations reported without reference to animals. Draft's claim stands; it does confirm model_filed=true for NHP and F9-knockout-mouse models, not for dogs.
rule_questions: Model switch (question #12): when the class moved from AAV2/dog to scAAV8/macaque, does the 2006 contra persist on the strip, or does status follow the new best model? 'Status of the BEST model as of a year' supports the latter; 'contra overrides every matched status' is ambiguous across models. Proposed reading: status follows the model in use, so engagement and efficacy read untested 1999 / contra 2006 / same 2014. If #12 resolves that contra is sticky per context, both 2014 entries revert to contra and the macaque match goes in the note.

Self-made juxtaposition: the draft scores safety 2006 contra on a juxtaposition (comparison_stated=false) yet declines to score the macaque per-dose gap, also a juxtaposition (same group, same product, same 2x10^12 dose). Either both count (then dose 2014 contra, off_by_>5x) or neither (then safety contra moves to 2007 on Mingozzi). Rule 1 says neither; recommended.

Dose cell for gene therapy: does 'specific activity consistent with preclinical' (potency per unit antigen) satisfy 'exposure target held'? Strict: no (dose untested). Lenient: yes (same 2017). The brief does not say; I applied strict.

Efficacy readout: is FIX activity an acceptable efficacy surrogate when no bleeding outcome is compared (Manno 2006) and the model is non-hemophilic (macaques, Nathwani 2014)? If not, the efficacy cell collapses to untested throughout; no hemophilic-animal-vs-patient bleeding comparison was found.

Is the intramuscular AAV2-FIX route inside this context ('FIX gene therapy, AAV')? The draft is inconsistent: efficacy opens on the IM dog paper but the context note says liver-directed. The answer decides whether Kay 2000 / Manno 2003 are missing entries.

model_filed: the draft sets true on every entry. FDA Hemgenix SBRA names NHP and F9-knockout mouse studies for the class, but no FDA/EMA document names the Chapel Hill dog / AAV2 model (never filed). Should model_filed be per-model (null/false for dog entries) rather than per-class?
